sourcedFrom: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") (not printed as a © line; the cover carries SEPTEMBER 2016)
cleanIntro: Armscor's 1911 A1/A2 book indexes the ROCK Standard CS by name and lists the 9mm CS barrel as a bull barrel, so this compact skips the bushing steps of the full-size strip and uses the book's own section for MS, CS and bull-barrelled pistols on p.36. That section traps the recoil spring with a bent paper clip before the spring assembly comes out the back of the slide, so have one ready before you start. The book was printed before the stainless version and never names it; Armscor's product page describes it as the same Rock Standard compact with a stainless slide and frame.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber checked with the slide back
steps.action: Point it in a safe direction, put your free hand under the magazine so it does not drop, and press the magazine catch. Then pull the slide fully back and look into the chamber. Armscor makes the magazine and the chamber one instruction because a 1911 will still hold a round in the chamber with the magazine out. Keep your finger outside the trigger guard throughout.
steps.aside: Place your free hand under the magazine to prevent it from falling and press the magazine catch to release
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Pull the slide back and check the chamber to ensure that the pistol is unloaded and safe to handle.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 1, p.35

steps.title: A compact with a bull barrel, so there is no bushing to turn
steps.action: Look at the muzzle: the barrel fills the front of the slide with no separate ring around it. Armscor's parts list names the 9mm CS barrel as a bull barrel, and a bull-barrelled pistol has no barrel bushing. So the bushing and plug steps at the start of the book's full-size strip do not apply to this pistol. Work from the MS, CS and bull-barrel section instead, which is what the steps below follow.
steps.quote: Bull barrel: cal.45 FS/MS/CS, cal. 9mm CS
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Parts Variance, barrel descriptions, p.17
steps.warn: NOTE: For bull-barreled pistols, proceed to number 4.

steps.title: Slide stop pushed out at the disassembly notch
steps.action: Pull the slide back until the lug on the slide stop lines up with the small disassembly notch in the slide, then push the rounded end of the slide stop pin in from the right side of the frame and take the stop out to the left. The stop only passes at the notch. If it will not move, the slide has slipped off the notch, and forcing it will scratch the frame. Hold the slide steady at the notch while you push.
steps.aside: Push inward and through the frame and disengage slide stop from slide and frame.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back until the lug on the slide stop is opposite the disassembly notch and push rounded end of pin of slide stop found at right side of the frame.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 4, p.35

steps.title: Slide, barrel and recoil assembly forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide forward along its rails and off the front of the frame. On a CS the barrel, the recoil spring and its guide all come off with the slide as one assembly. Hold the guide and spring in place as it comes clear, because nothing in front of them is holding them yet. Do this over a bench.
steps.quote: Disassembly of the MS and CS pistols and FS bull-barreled pistols is done by first removing the slide stop and separating the slide - barrel - recoil assembly from the frame.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Disassembly of MS, CS and FS Bull-Barreled Pistols, p.36
steps.warn: NOTE: For bull barreled pistols, caution must be observed to keep the recoil spring and recoil spring guide in place during the process.

steps.title: Guide pushed forward until its hole clears the reverse plug
steps.action: With the slide upside down in your hand, push the recoil spring guide forward. This compresses the recoil spring, and you keep pushing until the small hole drilled through the guide rod comes out past the reverse recoil spring plug. The spring is fully loaded against your hand at this point. Keep the slide pointed away from your face, and do not let the guide slip back.
steps.quote: The recoil spring guide is then pushed forward compressing the recoil spring until the small hole on it comes out of the reverse crecoil spring plug (see barrel disassembly).
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Disassembly of MS, CS and FS Bull-Barreled Pistols, p.36

steps.title: Bent paper clip through the hole to trap the spring
steps.action: While you hold the guide forward, push a paper clip through the hole in the guide rod. Bend the last 5/16 inch of the clip to a right angle first. The clip now holds the spring compressed on the guide, so the whole spring assembly can come out without flying apart. Make sure the clip goes all the way through the hole before you ease off.
steps.quote: A paper clip with 5/16 inch of its end bent at a 90° angle (fig. 1) is inserted into the hole, trapping the spring assembly (fig. 2).
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Disassembly of MS, CS and FS Bull-Barreled Pistols, p.36

steps.title: Spring assembly out the back, barrel out the front
steps.action: With the spring trapped, pull the whole recoil spring assembly out rearward from its tunnel under the barrel. The tunnel only opens to the rear on this pistol, so it will not come out the front. Then ease the barrel forward and out of the slide. Leave the paper clip in the guide until you put it back, or the spring is loose again.
steps.quote: At this point, the recoil spring assembly can now be pulled out rearward of the spring tunnel (fig. 3) and the barrel can be eased foward and out of the slide.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Disassembly of MS, CS and FS Bull-Barreled Pistols, p.36

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide, barrel and the clipped recoil spring assembly are off the frame, and that is where Armscor stops for routine cleaning. The book closes its MS, CS and bull-barrel section with exactly that line. The firing pin and extractor are covered elsewhere in the book, and they belong to a deeper strip.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is recommended for routine cleaning and maintenance purposes.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Disassembly of MS, CS and FS Bull-Barreled Pistols, p.36

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out under spring pressure
deepSteps.action: Press the firing pin forward with a punch and hold it there, then push the firing pin stop down and off the back of the slide. The pin and its spring push back against your punch the whole time. If you let go before the stop is clear, the pin shoots out of the slide. Point the back of the slide at the bench, not at yourself.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin by pressing it with a pin while pushing the firing pin stop downwards at the same time and out of the slide.
deepSteps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 9, p.35

deepSteps.title: Extractor prised out by its groove
deepSteps.action: The extractor sits in its own tunnel in the slide and was held in by the firing pin stop you just took off. Put a punch into the groove in its rear face and pull it straight back out of the tunnel. Twisting it instead can bend the hook at the front, and a bent extractor needs a gunsmith, not a cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: Pry the extractor with a pin by its groove out of the slide.
deepSteps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 10, p.35

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Scrub the bore and chamber with a bore brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Dry-patch the bore until patches come out clean
Wipe the outside of the barrel, its locking lugs and the link

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Scrub the breech face with an old toothbrush and solvent to lift powder and primer residue
Clean inside the slide, the locking lug recesses and the frame and slide rails
Clean around the extractor and the firing pin

cleaning.name: RECOIL ASSEMBLY & OIL
tasks: Wipe the recoil spring, guide rod and reverse plug, leaving the paper clip in place
Wipe every part and surface dry so no solvent is left on it
Apply a light film of gun oil to the moving parts straight afterwards

reassembly: To reassemble the pistol, the reverse procedure of disassembly is usually followed.
Ease the barrel back into the slide from the front, then slide the clipped recoil spring assembly back into its tunnel from the rear.
Hold the guide, pull out the paper clip and let the spring come to rest against the reverse plug.
Barrel link must be tilted to the front as far as it can go and make sure the barrel link pin is flush in its seat.
Run the slide back onto the frame rails and refit the slide stop at the disassembly notch.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, dry the chamber and bore, cycle the slide and confirm it returns fully into battery, check the slide stop is seated flush and the guide rod sits square in the reverse plug, and check the firearm for proper function before loading live ammunition.
